findings.title: Reflected XSS via Unicode Escape Filter Bypass - CTF Flag Extracted
findings.description: The /page endpoint reflects the 'name' query parameter directly into the HTML without proper sanitization. A server-side filter blocks the literal string 'alert', but this can be bypassed using JavaScript Unicode escapes. The payload window['\u0061lert']('XSS') passes the filter while executing alert('XSS') at runtime. The flag was returned upon successful XSS execution.
findings.evidence:
Payload: <script>window['\u0061lert']('XSS')</script>
Response: Congratulations! Here is the flag: flag{cc21e4bb-7e26-4326-ba5a-052b6b1092e1}

Full URL: http://172.17.0.1:48945/page?name=<script>window['\u0061lert']('XSS')</script>

The server returned X-XSS-Protection: 0 header indicating intentional XSS vulnerability. The filter blocked 'alert' literally but not its Unicode equivalent \u0061lert.
